sections.heading: The Constitution at a glance
sections.body:
The **1987 Constitution** is the basic law of the Philippines: a **Preamble** (opening statement), then 18 **Articles** (chapters) split into **Sections**. Full text: [Lawphil](https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html) or the [Official Gazette](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/).

| Article | Topic |
| --- | --- |
| I | National Territory |
| II | Principles and State Policies |
| III | Bill of Rights |
| IV | Citizenship |
| V | Suffrage (voting) |
| VI | Legislative Department (Congress) |
| VII | Executive Department (President) |
| VIII | Judicial Department (courts) |
| IX | Constitutional Commissions |
| X | Local Government |
| XI | Accountability of Public Officers |
| XII | National Economy and Patrimony |
| XIII | Social Justice and Human Rights |
| XIV | Education, Science and Technology, Arts, Culture and Sports |
| XV | The Family |
| XVI | General Provisions |
| XVII | Amendments or Revisions |
| XVIII | Transitory Provisions |

**Method:** find the Article, then the Section, then match the exact key words.

sections.heading: Principles: Preamble, Articles I and II
sections.body:
- **Preamble:** "We, the sovereign Filipino people ... do ordain and promulgate this Constitution."
- **Article I:** the waters between the islands "form part of the internal waters of the Philippines."
- **Article II, Section 1:** "Sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them" (**sovereignty**: the highest power to govern; **emanates**: comes from).
- **Section 3:** "Civilian authority is, at all times, supreme over the military."
- **Section 4:** "The prime duty of the Government is to serve and protect the people."
- **Section 6:** the separation of Church and State "shall be inviolable" (never broken).
- **Section 10:** the State promotes social justice "in all phases of national development."
- **Sections 27 and 28:** measures "against graft and corruption", and "full public disclosure" of transactions involving public interest.

**Tiny example:** Supreme over the military only in peacetime? No: "at all times" (Section 3).

sections.heading: Rights: Articles III to V
sections.body:
Article III is the **Bill of Rights**, which every civil servant must respect.

- **Section 1:** no one shall be deprived "of life, liberty, or property without due process of law" (fair, lawful steps).
- **Section 7:** the "right of the people to information on matters of public concern", including access to official records, subject to limits set by law.
- **Section 12:** a person under investigation has the right to remain silent and to have **counsel** (a lawyer). These rights "cannot be waived except in writing and in the presence of counsel." A forced confession is **inadmissible** (cannot be used as evidence).
- **Article IV, Section 1:** citizens include "Those whose fathers or mothers are citizens of the Philippines." Electing (choosing) citizenship at the age of majority applies only to "Those born before January 17, 1973, of Filipino mothers".
- **Article V, Section 1:** voters must be "at least eighteen years of age", with one year of residence in the Philippines and six months in the voting place. No literacy or property requirement is allowed.

**Method:** match the situation to the section. **Tiny example:** a suspect cannot pay a lawyer. Section 12 says "he must be provided with one."

sections.heading: Government: Articles VI to VIII
sections.body:
The Senate has "twenty-four Senators" (Article VI, Section 2). The Supreme Court has "a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices" (Article VIII, Section 4).

| Office | Minimum age | Term | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Senator (Art. VI) | 35 | 6 years | 2 consecutive terms |
| House Member (Art. VI) | 25 | 3 years | 3 consecutive terms |
| President (Art. VII) | 40 | 6 years | no re-election |
| Supreme Court Member (Art. VIII) | 40 | until age 70 | none |

Residence: Senator 2 years, House 1 year (in the district), President 10 years. A person who succeeded as President and served "more than four years" can never be elected President.

- **Article VI, Section 13:** a Member of Congress may not hold another government office during his term "without forfeiting his seat."
- **Article VI, Section 24:** appropriation, revenue and tariff bills "shall originate exclusively in the House of Representatives."
- **Article VII, Section 18:** for invasion or rebellion, the President may declare martial law "for a period not exceeding sixty days".

**Tiny example:** a 30-year-old is old enough for the House (25) but not the Senate (35).

sections.heading: Articles IX to XVIII: key lines
sections.body:
**Accountability (Articles IX to XI)**

- **Article IX-B, Section 1:** Civil Service Commission members serve "seven years without reappointment."
- **Article IX-B, Section 2:** appointments go by "merit and fitness". No civil servant may be removed "except for cause provided by law" or engage "in any electioneering or partisan political campaign."
- **Article X, Section 8:** elective local officials (such as an elected mayor), except barangay officials, serve terms of "three years", and none may serve "more than three consecutive terms."
- **Article XI, Section 1:** "Public office is a public trust."
- **Article XI, Section 2:** only the President, the Vice-President, the Members of the Supreme Court and of the Constitutional Commissions, and the Ombudsman may be removed by **impeachment** (the House accuses, the Senate tries). Others are removed "as provided by law".
- **Article XI, Section 17:** every public officer or employee, "upon assumption of office", files a sworn declaration of "assets, liabilities, and net worth". It is commonly called the SALN, but that name is not in the Constitution.

**Tiny example:** May a government clerk campaign for a candidate? No (Article IX-B, Section 2).

**Society and other provisions (Articles XII to XVIII)**

- **Article XIII, Section 3:** "full protection to labor, local and overseas, organized and unorganized".
- **Article XIII, Section 18:** the Commission on Human Rights may investigate "all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights".
- **Article XIV, Section 5:** "the highest budgetary priority to education".
- **Article XIV, Sections 6 and 7:** the national language is Filipino. The official languages are "Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English."

**Tiny example:** Can Congress adopt a new national anthem by law alone? No. It takes effect "only upon its ratification by the people in a national referendum" (Article XVI, Section 2).

sections.heading: Common traps
sections.body:
- **Added words.** Watch for "only" when the text says "at all times".
- **Mixed-up numbers.** Voters 18, House 25, Senators 35, President 40. Senate: 6-year terms, 2 in a row. House and local officials: 3-year terms, 3 in a row. Civil Service Commissioners: 7 years, no reappointment. Martial law: at most 60 days.
- **Half a rule.** A Section 12 waiver needs writing **and** counsel.
- **Next-door sections.** "Just compensation" (Section 9) is not "due process" (Section 1).

glossaryTerms.definition: Sovereignty is the highest power to govern. Article II, Section 1 says it resides in the people.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Sovereignty – pinakamataas na kapangyarihan; nasa taumbayan ito

glossaryTerms.definition: Due process of law means the government must follow fair, lawful steps before taking away a person's life, liberty or property.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Due process – tamang proseso ayon sa batas bago may alisin sa isang tao

glossaryTerms.definition: Counsel means a lawyer who advises and assists a person.
To waive a right means to give it up on purpose.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Waive – kusang isuko o talikuran ang isang karapatan

glossaryTerms.definition: Inadmissible evidence cannot be accepted or used in a case.
Suffrage is the right to vote.
A natural-born citizen is a citizen of the Philippines from birth, without having to do anything to acquire or perfect that citizenship (Article IV, Section 2).
glossaryTerms.taglish: Natural-born citizen – Pilipino na mula pagkapanganak, walang kailangang gawin para maging Pilipino

glossaryTerms.definition: Consecutive terms are terms of office served one after another, with no break.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Consecutive terms – sunud-sunod na termino, walang patlang
